summary: GRAVEYARD discovery pass covered every company in Chief's 12-name active T0 batch and rechecked current discovery/source state. The batch remains dominated by AI-compute, interconnect, foundry/equipment and data-center-power exposures, creating a shared capex/regulatory regime that can hide cross-company correlation. Fresh primary evidence sharpened several weak-signal paths: Rocket Lab's acquisition/Neutron capital path, Astera's Amazon performance warrants, NVIDIA/ASML China-export constraints, TSMC overseas-fab margin dilution, Micron's expanded U.S. fab build, and Vertiv backlog optionality/cancellation risk. However, the open discovery-cadence directive is not cleared: FINRA is fresh only at partition level with eventDataAvailable=false, and all cadence-due active gating discovery families were not independently completed in this run. Sensor gaps remain non-gating but visible. Lane is not ready for Chief approval.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: The company now highlights an Iridium acquisition path while Neutron remains a major development program; financing and integration can become a second-order bottleneck independent of launch demand.
contradictions: Backlog and strategic expansion support demand, but acquisition plus launch-vehicle development increases capital-allocation complexity.
unknowns: Exact acquisition cash bridge after closing, Neutron qualification schedule and incremental financing need.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Acquisition funding closes without material dilution/leverage stress and Neutron qualification milestones remain on schedule with stable cash runway.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: Latest filing shows very rapid growth but continued revenue dependence on a limited customer set; broadening customer count, not headline growth, is the weak-signal variable to watch.
contradictions: Strong growth/net income coexist with concentrated hyperscaler exposure.
unknowns: True end-customer diversification behind ODM/module channels and hyperscaler insourcing path.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Top-customer share declines materially while aggregate growth remains strong across multiple independent end customers.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: Amazon-linked warrant tranches vest against up to $6.5B of purchases, creating unusually explicit customer-demand validation but also a customer-linked dilution/contra-revenue mechanism worth tracking as a precursor signal.
contradictions: The warrant validates potential scale while simultaneously increasing dependence on one customer's purchasing trajectory.
unknowns: Future vesting cadence, realized customer mix outside Amazon-linked demand and exact fully diluted impact at scale.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Warrant vesting remains limited while non-Amazon design wins diversify revenue faster than the purchase milestones concentrate it.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: China data-center access remains policy-constrained even after limited H200 licensing; the weak signal is ecosystem substitution in restricted markets rather than only lost current-quarter revenue.
contradictions: Global AI demand remains exceptional while a large strategic market can accelerate local substitutes.
unknowns: Long-run share migration to custom accelerators and China-local ecosystems.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: NVIDIA regains durable compliant access and restricted-market ecosystem share stops shifting to alternatives.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: Data Center revenue growth is strong and MI350 demand is visible, but the weak signal to monitor is repeat production breadth across customers rather than first-wave deployments.
contradictions: High growth supports product validation while durable accelerator share remains less proven than CPU share.
unknowns: MI-series buyer concentration, repeat-deployment cadence and software switching costs.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Multiple independent customers expand MI-series deployments across successive quarters with stable economics.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: Top-five end customers represented roughly 45% of revenue in the cited quarter; bespoke AI silicon can strengthen strategic positioning while quietly increasing dependence on a handful of giant buyers.
contradictions: Custom silicon depth raises moat and switching costs, but customers retain extreme bargaining power and program concentration.
unknowns: Per-customer AI program durability and future mix after VMware integration.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: AI revenue scales while top-customer share falls and no single program dominates incremental growth.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: Overseas redundancy is becoming a structural second-order cost: management has guided to multi-year margin dilution from overseas fabs even as geographic diversification reduces single-region concentration risk.
contradictions: Resilience investment reduces geopolitical concentration but structurally raises cost versus Taiwan fabs.
unknowns: Long-run overseas yield/cost convergence and customer willingness to pay a resilience premium.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Overseas fabs converge to Taiwan economics faster than guided without sacrificing utilization or customer commitments.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: China represented 29.1% of 2025 net sales, so export-control changes remain a material discovery sensor even while EUV demand is strong; supplier concentration is still an under-observed dependency.
contradictions: Near-monopoly lithography economics coexist with policy exposure outside company control.
unknowns: Current critical-supplier concentration and exact 2026 China mix under new restrictions.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: China mix declines without order loss and supplier redundancy improves without material cost/lead-time penalties.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: Related-party revenue rose sharply and top five customers represented 57% of FY2026 revenue; SoftBank/Arm China relationship changes are therefore operational weak signals, not merely governance footnotes.
contradictions: Asset-light royalty economics are diversified across devices but financial reporting remains concentrated in a small customer set.
unknowns: Incremental AGI CPU economics, Arm China governance durability and SoftBank-linked commercial dependence.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Related-party share normalizes while external royalty growth broadens across independent licensees.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: Micron raised planned U.S. investment above $250B through 2035; fab construction is now itself a capital-cycle signal that can preserve HBM scarcity or later amplify supply if demand normalizes.
contradictions: Domestic capacity improves resilience while creating a large fixed-cost/capex commitment into a historically cyclical market.
unknowns: HBM4 competitor yields, contract floors and normalized capex intensity after current buildout.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Capacity additions remain demand-matched with sustained HBM pricing/margins and no material balance-sheet stress.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: Strong AI-networking growth and XPO innovation are positive, but historical Microsoft/Meta concentration means architecture decisions at a few cloud titans remain the critical weak signal.
contradictions: Product innovation broadens the platform while a few buyers still can swing growth materially.
unknowns: Current 2026 top-customer shares and adoption breadth for XPO/1.6T products.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Customer concentration declines materially while new optical/networking products scale across multiple large buyers.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: Backlog reached about $15B at year-end 2025, but filings explicitly state orders may be cancelled/rescheduled and recent acquisitions may carry differing termination rights. Backlog composition is therefore a discovery variable, not a static quality metric.
contradictions: Demand is visibly strong while conversion timing and cancellation rights can still impair realized revenue.
unknowns: Backlog aging, customer concentration and cancellation/reschedule rates by acquired versus legacy business.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Backlog converts on schedule with low cancellation/reschedule rates through multiple quarters and broader customer mix.

materialFindings.finding: AI-infrastructure batch concentration is itself a discovery blind spot: nominal company diversity masks exposure to the same hyperscaler capex, export-policy and power-buildout regime.

Explicit customer-linked economic mechanisms are emerging as high-value weak-signal monitors: Astera's Amazon performance warrant, Broadcom concentration, ARM related-party/customer concentration and Arista cloud-titan concentration.

Current automated-source health is 4/4 healthy for required probes, but FINRA only proves partition freshness and explicitly has eventDataAvailable=false; this cannot clear the open discovery-cadence directive.

contradictions: Healthy endpoint/probe status is not equivalent to complete event-level discovery acquisition.
Geographic resilience investments at TSMC and Micron may reduce supply-chain fragility while increasing structural cost/capital intensity.
unknowns: All cadence-due active gating discovery families were not independently cleared in this run.
FINRA current-event rows remain unavailable from the machine probe because eventDataAvailable=false.
No reliable universe-wide independent patent/hiring/facility sweep was completed for all active-batch names in this cycle.

peerRequests.request: Keep FINRA capability vs freshness fail-closed and verify which cadence-due active gating discovery families still require same-cycle manual acquisition.
Normalize customer-linked concentration mechanisms for ALAB, AVGO, ARM and ANET and backlog composition for RKLB/VRT before promotion.
Model overseas-fab resilience premium/cost at TSM and long-run memory-capacity feedback at MU as successor constraints.

accuracyDebates.reason: Warrants, related-party sales and concentrated custom programs can reveal dependency earlier than aggregate revenue trends.
Order value without cancellation/aging terms overstates durability.
